title: Constellation cadence and budget handoff
summary: Quarterly cadence reset and budget handoff for Q2; leadership updates on hiring posture, platform reliability work, and product roadmap tradeoffs. Finance outlines revised headcount budget and contingency; engineering shares SLO improvements and technical debt plan. Open Q&A and action items with owners.
topics: Hiring freeze contingencies and RIF rumors
action_items: Evelyn Cho - circulate Q2 budget workbook and scenario sheets - due 2026-03-12
Jordan Reed - publish engineering tech-debt roadmap highlights to Console and Slack - due 2026-03-16
Sofia Alvarez - update product prioritization doc with critical/optional flags and share with GTM - due 2026-03-11
Samir Patel - set up virtual town halls for people questions and 1:1 signups - due 2026-03-10
Liam Park - run two targeted SLO load tests with Dedicated config and share results - due 2026-03-20
next_steps: Finance to send budget scenarios and recording
Product and Eng to align on 6 'must-have' deliverables for Q2
People to schedule department-level deep dives next week
Leadership to confirm hiring freeze boundaries by Friday
transcript:
Header: All‑Hands - Constellation cadence and budget handoff
Date: 2026-03-09 17:00 UTC | Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees (list): Maya, Liam, Sofia, Jordan, Samir, Evelyn, Rene, Carlos + company-wide

-- Summary section (auto-generated, may be incomplete) --
Maya: High-level on posture + goals. Evelyn: budget scenarios. Liam/Jordan: infra and SLOs. Sofia: roadmap sharpen. Q&A and next steps.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. Um, quick housekeeping, recording's on, deck is in #all-hands — link in calendar. We'll keep to about 45-55 mins, leave time for Q&A.
00:18 Maya: So main purpose today is to hand off Q2 budget, to be transparent about choices, and to align on cadence adjustments. I'll go first then Evelyn will go through the numbers.
00:35 Evelyn: Hi team. Thanks. I'll be quick: high level we have three scenarios — baseline, conservative, and aggressive. Baseline assumes flat spend with some reallocation toward Dedicated capacity and reliability work. Conservative reduces new hires by 30% and holds runway to 18 months. Aggressive allows for the hiring plan we published last quarter.
01:05 Evelyn: Important note — we are deliberately keeping runway language simple. We recommend the baseline for now, but we need leadership sign-off on role prioritization.
01:28 Jordan: Can I ask about the Dedicated pools line item? Are we shifting more capex into Dedicated or is this an ops reallocation?
01:35 Evelyn: It's primarily ops (reserved capacity contracts), not capex. We will re-balance cloud credits and reserved capacity. There's a small one-off for initial onboarding for two private customers.
01:52 Liam: On the reliability side, we are proposing a 6-week initiative to close top-10 P0 flakiness triggers — this will slightly increase infra spend but reduce incident MTTR and token loss. We think it's accretive to revenue.
02:12 Sofia: From product, our ask is clear: keep budget for the two initiatives that unlock self-serve adoption — the 'faststart' templates and improved Console onboarding. Those move the needle on PLG funnel.
02:28 Maya: Great. A few contextual decisions — we will prioritize customer-facing product for self-serve (faststart) and the SLO/reliability project. Hiring will be prioritized for infra/engineering roles and two senior product hires. Everything else is on hold pending role-by-role review.
02:54 Samir: To be transparent on people, no blanket hiring freeze announced yet — we're doing role-level triage. We'll share criteria and a short form to submit open reqs for prioritization. We also know there's anxiety around "freeze" rumors; we're setting up town halls.
03:14 Rene: Quick micro ask — can we get clarity on ramp timeline for new SEs if we shift to more Dedicated customers? That impacts capacity planning.
03:24 Jordan: Good point. We will publish ramp metrics. Short answer: plan for 6-8 week onboarding under current plan.

05:00 Liam: Ok technical deep-dive moment — SLO progress. We improved p99 latency on hosted API by 12% last sprint via KV cache tweaks and batch routing changes. But we have a regression on 8k token long-form paths with some quantization combos — tracking that.
05:25 Carlos: The long-form regression looks tied to kernel selection when quantized models hit sequences > 4k; we'll run more coverage.
05:38 Liam: Yes, and as a mitigant we suggest fallback to non-quantized variant for long sessions in the routing policy. Tradeoff is cost vs latency.
05:50 Evelyn: Finance: what's the delta if we keep non-quantized fallbacks?
05:56 Liam: Roughly a 15% per-token cost increase on those sessions, but it preserves p99 SLA.
06:08 Maya: Ok, high level decision framing: prefer service quality for tiered customers, allow cost-optimized for PLG unless they choose otherwise. We'll put that in the policy doc.

08:00 Sofia: On roadmap — we are narrowing to 6 top deliverables for Q2: faststart templates, Console onboarding revamp, reliability initiative (SLOs), Dedicated autoscale improvements, deployment shims for Private customers, and cost-optimizer profiles. The rest are lower priority.
08:20 Samir: We'll need org-level sign-off because some teams will have hiring impacts.

10:00 Crowd murmur / applause (shoutouts)
10:10 Maya: Quick shoutouts — shout to DevRel for the new reference app; Product Design for the Console microcopy sprint. Also to Ops for 99.95 last month.

12:00 Q&A open (typed questions via Slack + mic)
12:20 Employee (anon): Are layoffs on the table? Heard from recruiters that something's happening.
12:30 Maya: Short answer: no company-wide layoffs planned. We are doing prioritization. If anything changes, we will communicate quickly and directly. We're legal-bound to consult.
12:55 Samir: We're focused on redeployment before reductions where possible, and we will provide 1:1 support.
13:15 Employee: Will hiring slow affect contractor conversion?
13:20 Samir: Yes, slows this quarter; exceptions possible for mission-critical roles. We'll publish criteria.

15:00 Engineering metric callout
15:10 Jordan: Our incident cadence is down month-over-month, but there's still a long tail of flakey downstreams. Proposed action: two-week reliability blitz then monthly retros to keep momentum.
15:35 Maya: Sounds right. Pairing with finance makes sense because there will be a short-term spend bump.

18:00 Finance detail walkthrough (Evelyn shares a screen; note: some numbers transcribed imperfectly)
18:20 Evelyn: Baseline headcount: 150 -> projected 165 by EOY under baseline, conservative projects 150 remain steady. Hiring ask list will be a prioritized spreadsheet with green/amber/red flags.
18:45 Evelyn: We also modeled a scenario where we pause non-critical hiring and still hit product deadlines by pushing some features to Q3. We'll publish the workbook.
19:10 Employee: What's the runway in months on conservative?
19:15 Evelyn: ~18 months, assuming current ARR growth and steady churn.

22:00 Questions about sales & GTM impact
22:12 Rene: If we deprioritize low-conversion roadmap items, what's the messaging to customers?
22:22 Sofia: We'll be explicit in release notes and proactively shepherd customers likely to be impacted; for Dedicated/Private customers we'll offer migration windows.

25:00 Short technical clarification (mild crosstalk)
25:30 Liam: There's also a small engineering ask to pause one refactor that has risk to latency; we'll move that to Q3.
25:45 Jordan: We'll add that to the tech-debt list so it's visible to ENG+Prod.

28:00 People ops Qs
28:12 Samir: We will run several small town halls and open office hours. Compensation is not being changed at this time. We're reviewing open role priorities with managers.

30:00 Security/compliance reminder
30:10 Maya: Quick note — SOC2 re-audit coming. Security team will send checklist. Any teams with hosted customers please respond to attestations within 5 business days.
30:28 Employee: Slack question — will audit logs be longer retention for enterprise?
30:35 Sofia: That's in the roadmap for Private customers; retention add-on will be a paid feature.

33:00 Open mic highlights
33:10 Employee (Carlos): Want to flag that the Dedicated autoscaler has some edge cases with preemptible VMs - it sometimes ramps too slow.
33:26 Liam: Yes, thanks — we'll prioritize that in the autoscale improvements item.

36:00 Short demo clip (Console microcopy & onboarding flow) — applause
36:40 Sofia: One thing to call out — the new onboarding reduces time-to-first-call by ~40% in our shadow tests. Caveat: sample size small.
36:55 Maya: Great. That's the kind of win we keep funded.

39:00 Finance callouts & approvals needed
39:12 Evelyn: Need sign-off on the baseline by EOD Friday to start key hires. If we don't have sign-off we'll fall to conservative and pause non-critical roles.
39:30 Maya: We'll aim to confirm by Friday after role-by-role calls.

41:00 Q&A wrap and rumor control
41:15 Employee (anon): If the conservative path triggers, will severance be better than industry baseline?
41:28 Maya: We will follow a policy that protects folks — severance and support packages will be competitive, but again, we're not planning reductions at this point.

43:00 Rapid fire updates from teams (30s each)
43:10 DevRel: reference app out, 2 case studies in pipeline
43:50 Security: SOC2 checklist next week
44:15 Sales: pipeline healthy; a few large deals expecting Q2 close
44:40 Support: NPS up 3 points after KB revamp
45:10 Infra: rolling kernel upgrades, no planned downtime

47:00 Leadership closing remarks
47:05 Maya: Thank you. Key takeaways — we prioritize reliability and self-serve product; role-level hiring triage not an immediate freeze; finance will push workbook; town halls for people questions. Expect transparency and concrete timelines.
47:30 Liam: Engineering will publish technical debt and SLO plan and schedule the reliability blitz.
47:45 Evelyn: I'll share budget scenarios and the recording after this call.
47:52 Samir: People ops will send sign-up for 1:1 and group Q&A.

50:00 Final Q&A and sign-off (chat continues after recording stops)
50:12 Employee: Thanks.
50:15 Maya: Thanks everyone. End.

-- End of transcript --

Notes on transcription quality: several screen-shared numeric tables were summarized; a few product names may be inaccurate or slightly garbled (e.g., "faststart" might appear as "fast start"). Some speaker labels are approximated during cross-talk.

References mentioned (not included): Q2 budget workbook (link), Console onboarding deck (link), tech-debt spreadsheet (link), SOC2 checklist (link).
